bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

bull_bear.body:
- Portfolio diversification across eight divisions and two near-equally sized segments (50.5 per cent and 49.5 per cent of revenue) serving different demand cycles, so a difficult period in one half is ordinarily cushioned by the other - cited as the principal reason the earnings line has risen in each of the last four years.
- Fully integrated engineering capability - design, tooling, manufacturing, project management and erection are held in-house, allowing a customer to present a functional requirement rather than a drawing and receive a commissioned asset.
- Deliberate mix management: roughly 65 to 70 per cent of revenue comes from prioritised businesses growing materially above the Company average, while the remaining 30 to 35 per cent receives no growth capital and is allowed to decline; margin expansion has followed from mix change rather than pricing.
- US manufacturing footprint (Tennessee and Alabama) means the largest American revenue stream, metal buildings, is made within the United States and was not exposed to import tariff action - a different risk profile from cross-border shipment.
- Long growth runway in the United States: the addressable metal buildings and components market exceeds USD 10 billion a year and the Company's share is under 3 per cent, with the binding constraint being plant location rather than customer acceptance.
- Eight management system certifications spanning general quality, environment, occupational health and safety, welding, rail, automotive and aerospace - certification being a condition of entry to several industries served.
- Engineering services bills predominantly on a project outcome basis rather than man hours, so AI-assisted design productivity gains accrue to the Company rather than the customer, while engineering judgement and the statutory professional engineer's certification are not amenable to automation.
- Validation laboratories, material testing protocols and precision-led processes hold output to a common standard across locations, allowing the Company to serve global supply chains from more than one geography.
- Long-standing marquee customer relationships across verticals - Reliance, JSW Steel, Toyo Engineering, MRO Air India and Powermech in PEB; WABCO, Emerson, Endurance, IFB and Xylem in industrial components; Toyota Boshoku, Thermax and ALF Engineering in precision tubes; Saint Gobain, Schaeffler and VECV in steel profiles.
- Industrial harmony and cost visibility: three-year wage agreements signed at the Chennai, Tarapur and Hyderabad plants, and the Best Management Award in the large scale category from the Labour Department, Government of Telangana for 2026.
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Commodity price risk - steel is the dominant input — Steel is both the principal input and the substrate of value addition, so the whole cost base moves with it; steel price volatility during FY26 was accentuated by energy price inflation and, per the MD&A threat list, commodity and energy price inflation aggravated by the West Asia conflict continues to pressure input costs and requires continuous pass-through. Mitigation is through price variation clauses in project contracts, pass-through pricing and inventory planning - which are contractual and timing devices, not immunity, and an inventory build ahead of announced price increases was itself a working-capital cost during the year.
- Working capital and receivables intensity inherent to project-led businesses — Named a Weakness in the SWOT and a Threat in its own right (elevated working capital intensity with attendant borrowing costs). At the year end net working capital stood at 82 days of revenue against the Company's own 75-day target, receivables increased by Rs 151 crore with a portion tied to project sites awaiting handover formalities, and debtor days moved from 65 to 66. Operating cash flow fell year on year specifically because of this working-capital absorption. Mitigation is a defined reduction programme targeting 75 days, site handover completion and collection focus.
- Leverage temporarily above the internal comfort level — Gross borrowings rose and the gross debt to equity ratio moved to 1.05 from 0.92, driven by about USD 14 million of acquisition funding for Ascent Structural plus working capital borrowing that scaled with revenue and a planned inventory build. Management calls this 'not a number we are comfortable with' and has committed to bringing it to 0.8 or below during FY 2026-27 through internal accruals, the promoter warrant infusion and working capital release. Net of record cash balances gearing was materially lower, but the commitment is unfulfilled and depends on three levers, only one of which is fully within management's control.
- Trade policy and tariff risk in export markets — Demonstrated rather than hypothetical: United States tariffs disrupted hydraulics export order flows during FY26 - described as the one place in the portfolio where trade policy had a direct effect on the business model - and the backlog fell to Rs 22 crore before recovering to about Rs 34 crore. The structural mitigation is that the largest American revenue stream, metal buildings, is manufactured within the United States and was therefore not exposed; the residual exposure sits in cross-border shipment, which the Company is diversifying towards Europe and West Asia.
- Labour availability and rising labour cost in both India and the United States — Also demonstrated: labour availability constrained fabrication throughput in Pre Engineered Buildings India in the earlier part of FY26, holding back output and deferring revenue. Resolution required a wider contractor network, wage benchmarking and buffer manning - and management states that securing that manning required paying more, which carries a modest cost to operating margin until automation matures. The Chairman frames the underlying structural issue as the narrowing of the labour cost arbitrage Indian manufacturing has long enjoyed. In the United States, senior management and engineering talent is described as expensive.
- Market cyclicality and competitive capacity additions, particularly in PEB — The businesses sit on infrastructure, construction and mobility cycles. The MD&A flags intensifying competition in PEB alongside industry capacity additions, which can pressure pricing in the short term. Mitigation is the two-segment, multi-vertical portfolio across geographies and end markets and the rising share of recurring OEM and services revenue - but the SWOT also concedes that scale in individual verticals sits below that of the largest single-vertical competitors.
- Currency and international concentration risk — A growing share of revenue and assets is denominated in US dollars and euros - international markets were 24.1 per cent of FY26 revenue, up from 20 per cent, and the overseas subsidiaries contributed Rs 959.62 crore. Mitigation is forward cover, natural hedges from local manufacture and monitoring of translation effects; FY26 recorded a favourable translation movement in other comprehensive income, which is a reminder that the movement can run the other way. The US buildings platform's growth also depends on a single demand theme - data centre and industrial construction - and is geographically confined to the South and Midwest by plant location.
- Regulatory risk - implementation of the Labour Codes — The four Labour Codes notified in November 2025 mark a structural reform of the employment law framework. The Company has assessed the indicative financial impact but the effect will only be given as final Central and State rules are notified, so the quantum and timing remain outside its control and the financial impact will be recognised as rules are finalised.

outlook.body:
- Run a deliberately balanced two-segment, eight-division portfolio serving independent demand cycles, so that a slowdown in one division is seldom a slowdown across the portfolio - stated to be by design, and cited as a principal reason the earnings line has risen in each of the last four years.
- Concentrate growth capital on 'prioritised' businesses, which are roughly 65 to 70 per cent of revenue and grow materially above the Company average, while giving no growth capital to legacy steel and solar EPC streams and allowing them to decline as a share of revenue; margin expansion is to come from mix change rather than pricing.
- Recycle capital away from non-prioritised businesses - the entire 51 per cent holding in the defence subsidiary was divested in September 2025 - and allocate capital only to businesses that earn their cost of capital and more.
- Scale the United States platform as the principal growth engine: manufacture within the United States from Tennessee and Alabama, extend from metal building systems into fabricated structural steel (Ascent Structural, acquired June 2025 for about USD 14 million), and grow through geographic reach rather than competitive displacement, since the constraint on the sub-3-per-cent share is plant location and not customer acceptance.
- Automate in response to a narrowing labour cost arbitrage: the AGT robotics welding line in the United States replaced work that previously absorbed twenty to thirty people per product with two, and painting, surface treatment and assembly are being automated in India.
- Be selective on order intake in PEB India, treating order intake as a margin decision before a volume decision - an order of approximately Rs 150 crore was declined during the year because the product mix did not meet the Company's requirements.
- Operate as a design-to-erection contractor rather than a component supplier, delivering turnkey building systems engineered to each customer's layout, process and safety codes, with in-house galvanising and a dedicated structural engineering group.
- Embed AI-assisted design and detailing into the engineering services delivery workflow, retaining the productivity gain because billing is predominantly project-outcome based rather than man-hour based, and invest in a dedicated United States sales infrastructure.
- Diversify the export base geographically - developing European customers in hydraulics after United States tariff disruption, and building a West Asia trading and distribution platform through Pennar FZCO's acquisition of Agile Traders.
- Address India's solar manufacturing expansion with limited capital, through the 45 per cent ZAP91 joint venture with Zetwerk and through supply of solar module mounting structures, with no further capital commitments to the venture envisaged.
- Reduce leverage and working capital intensity: bring the debt to equity ratio down to 0.8 or below during FY 2026-27 through internal accruals, the promoter warrant infusion and working capital release, and run a defined reduction programme targeting 75 net working capital days.
- Reinvest rather than distribute - the Company has been investing new capital to expand its product profile and markets, and the Directors are not recommending a dividend on equity shares.
- Source, process and test steel through common quality systems across divisions, giving purchasing leverage and consistency of material across product lines, and hold output to a common standard across locations through validation laboratories and material testing protocols.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: FY26 was a year of portfolio surgery rather than greenfield capacity building. The largest step was inorganic: in June 2025 the Company acquired the structural assets of Telco Enterprises in the United States for about USD 14 million, now operating as Ascent Structural LLC, which extends the American platform from metal building systems into fabricated structural steel and adds capacity in Alabama; Pennar Global Investments Alabama LLC was incorporated in the same month to hold the assets, and the business is already contributing to revenue. Automation was the second thrust: an AGT robotics welding line was commissioned in the United States, automating end plate fitment and stiffener welding - work that previously absorbed twenty to thirty people per product and now requires two, at higher precision and materially lower man hours per tonne - while in India automation was extended across painting, surface treatment and assembly, partly to address labour availability and cost. A dedicated Body in White plant for a marquee automotive customer (Hyundai) reached its final stages of completion during the year, with commissioning expected early in FY 2026-27, after which the vertical will scale as a long cycle OEM programme. At Raebareli, the Company's newest Indian plant, production was streamlined and output taken to the 1,200 MT mark, establishing it as the springboard for northern and eastern India; in PEB India capacity is being added in fabrication and painting lines with utilisation targeted at about 80 per cent against a 70 per cent exit for FY26. In the ZAP91 Solar India joint venture (45 per cent held, with Zetwerk) the Company made a final equity contribution to fund completion and commissioning of the solar module manufacturing plant at Sadashivpet, Telangana, targeted before 30 June 2026, with the module technology upgraded to the G12R format during project execution and no further capital commitment from Pennar envisaged. Two structural moves reshaped the perimeter: the entire 51 per cent holding in Enertech Pennar Defense and Engineering Systems Private Limited was divested in September 2025 as a non-prioritised business, and Pennar FZCO acquired Agile Traders FZCO in December 2025 to build a West Asia trading and distribution platform. Looking forward, planned capex for FY 2026-27 is deliberately light at under Rs 100 crore, principally the completion of the Body in White plant and further automation, to be funded from internal accruals.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Public capital expenditure in India remains the principal demand engine: the Union Budget for 2026-27 provides a capital outlay of Rs 12.22 lakh crore, up about 11.5 per cent, with Rs 2.81 lakh crore to Railways and Rs 3.10 lakh crore to Road Transport and Highways.
- Manufacturing gross value added grew 10.7 per cent and construction 7.4 per cent in FY26 - the two sectors that most directly drive demand for engineered steel products, pre engineered buildings, tubes and industrial components.
- The Indian pre engineered buildings market is projected by industry studies to grow at roughly 12 per cent a year over the coming decade, with demand broadening beyond warehousing and logistics into data centres, semiconductor and electronics fabrication, solar module plants, food processing and general manufacturing, aided by PLI schemes, PM Gati Shakti and state industrial corridor programmes.
- Speed of construction, cost certainty, superior quality control and sustainability continue to shift share from conventional construction towards factory fabricated steel buildings.
- The sustained United States capital expenditure cycle, led by data centres, manufacturing reshoring and industrial construction, continues to expand the addressable market for the metal buildings businesses; the addressable market exceeds USD 10 billion annually and data centre annualised spending crossed USD 50 billion, overtaking conventional office construction.
- Vehicle lightweighting, electrification and tightening crash and emission regulation are reshaping body structure requirements towards high strength and ultra high strength steels and modular architectures, playing directly to Body in White, hydraulics and precision tubes capabilities; the Indian auto component industry grew 12.7 per cent with OEM supplies up 16.3 per cent.
- Tightening emission norms and rising fuel costs favour energy efficient combustion technologies such as AFBC and waste heat recovery, sustaining replacement demand for boilers, waste heat recovery systems and heat exchangers across food processing, rice milling, chemicals, textiles, distilleries and metals.
- Indian Railways' sustained modernisation and capacity expansion programme, with a record capital outlay and an expanded pipeline of high speed corridors, dedicated freight infrastructure and modern rolling stock.
- AI-assisted design is reshaping engineering services economics by automating lower-end detailing man hours while raising the premium on engineering judgement, project management and statutory certification; because billing is project-outcome based, productivity gains accrue to the service provider - management views this as a structural tailwind rather than a threat.
- Mechanisation across construction, material handling, agriculture, mining and rail, with electro-hydraulic systems, IoT-enabled predictive maintenance and smart sensors, underpins hydraulics demand.
- India's solar build-out - a record 44 GW added in FY26 taking cumulative capacity to about 150 GW - with domestic module manufacturing scaling under the ALMM regime and production linked incentives.
- Margin lever: revenue mix migration towards prioritised, higher-margin businesses, with gross margins in the region of 42 to 43 per cent supported by value added mix despite commodity price inflation in the second half.
- Margin lever: operating leverage on a contained fixed cost base as capacity utilisation rises in PEB India and in the United States.
- Cost headwind flagged: securing PEB manning required paying more, which carries a modest cost to operating margin until automation matures; and the labour cost arbitrage Indian manufacturing has long enjoyed is narrowing.
- Steel price volatility, accentuated by energy price inflation, is managed through price variation clauses in the order book and pass-through pricing.
- Trade policy is a two-sided driver: tariff shifts in the United States affect exports, but manufacturing presence within the United States insulates the bulk of American revenue - the one affected stream, hydraulics, has recovered.
- Return on capital employed moderated as recently deployed capital, including the acquisition and the Body in White facility, is yet to contribute full-year earnings; the medium term objective of raising ROCE remains unchanged.
- Global growth is projected by the IMF to moderate to 3.1 per cent in 2026 before recovering to 3.2 per cent in 2027, with the near term outlook shaped by the conflict in West Asia and the resultant volatility in energy prices.
- Pre Engineered Buildings India closed FY26 with an order backlog of Rs 810 crore, with quote activity healthy and exit capacity utilisation of 70 per cent.
- The combined order backlog of Ascent Buildings and Ascent Structural in the United States stood at about USD 63 million at year end, having grown roughly 20 per cent in the closing three months of the year.

risks.note: Steel is both the principal input and the substrate of value addition, so the whole cost base moves with it; steel price volatility during FY26 was accentuated by energy price inflation and, per the MD&A threat list, commodity and energy price inflation aggravated by the West Asia conflict continues to pressure input costs and requires continuous pass-through. Mitigation is through price variation clauses in project contracts, pass-through pricing and inventory planning - which are contractual and timing devices, not immunity, and an inventory build ahead of announced price increases was itself a working-capital cost during the year.
risks.risk: Commodity price risk - steel is the dominant input

risks.note: Named a Weakness in the SWOT and a Threat in its own right (elevated working capital intensity with attendant borrowing costs). At the year end net working capital stood at 82 days of revenue against the Company's own 75-day target, receivables increased by Rs 151 crore with a portion tied to project sites awaiting handover formalities, and debtor days moved from 65 to 66. Operating cash flow fell year on year specifically because of this working-capital absorption. Mitigation is a defined reduction programme targeting 75 days, site handover completion and collection focus.
risks.risk: Working capital and receivables intensity inherent to project-led businesses

risks.note: Gross borrowings rose and the gross debt to equity ratio moved to 1.05 from 0.92, driven by about USD 14 million of acquisition funding for Ascent Structural plus working capital borrowing that scaled with revenue and a planned inventory build. Management calls this 'not a number we are comfortable with' and has committed to bringing it to 0.8 or below during FY 2026-27 through internal accruals, the promoter warrant infusion and working capital release. Net of record cash balances gearing was materially lower, but the commitment is unfulfilled and depends on three levers, only one of which is fully within management's control.
risks.risk: Leverage temporarily above the internal comfort level

risks.note: Demonstrated rather than hypothetical: United States tariffs disrupted hydraulics export order flows during FY26 - described as the one place in the portfolio where trade policy had a direct effect on the business model - and the backlog fell to Rs 22 crore before recovering to about Rs 34 crore. The structural mitigation is that the largest American revenue stream, metal buildings, is manufactured within the United States and was therefore not exposed; the residual exposure sits in cross-border shipment, which the Company is diversifying towards Europe and West Asia.
risks.risk: Trade policy and tariff risk in export markets

risks.note: Also demonstrated: labour availability constrained fabrication throughput in Pre Engineered Buildings India in the earlier part of FY26, holding back output and deferring revenue. Resolution required a wider contractor network, wage benchmarking and buffer manning - and management states that securing that manning required paying more, which carries a modest cost to operating margin until automation matures. The Chairman frames the underlying structural issue as the narrowing of the labour cost arbitrage Indian manufacturing has long enjoyed. In the United States, senior management and engineering talent is described as expensive.
risks.risk: Labour availability and rising labour cost in both India and the United States

risks.note: The businesses sit on infrastructure, construction and mobility cycles. The MD&A flags intensifying competition in PEB alongside industry capacity additions, which can pressure pricing in the short term. Mitigation is the two-segment, multi-vertical portfolio across geographies and end markets and the rising share of recurring OEM and services revenue - but the SWOT also concedes that scale in individual verticals sits below that of the largest single-vertical competitors.
risks.risk: Market cyclicality and competitive capacity additions, particularly in PEB

risks.note: A growing share of revenue and assets is denominated in US dollars and euros - international markets were 24.1 per cent of FY26 revenue, up from 20 per cent, and the overseas subsidiaries contributed Rs 959.62 crore. Mitigation is forward cover, natural hedges from local manufacture and monitoring of translation effects; FY26 recorded a favourable translation movement in other comprehensive income, which is a reminder that the movement can run the other way. The US buildings platform's growth also depends on a single demand theme - data centre and industrial construction - and is geographically confined to the South and Midwest by plant location.

The four Labour Codes notified in November 2025 mark a structural reform of the employment law framework. The Company has assessed the indicative financial impact but the effect will only be given as final Central and State rules are notified, so the quantum and timing remain outside its control and the financial impact will be recognised as rules are finalised.
risks.risk: Regulatory risk - implementation of the Labour Codes

currentContext.expansion: FY26 was a year of portfolio surgery rather than greenfield capacity building. The largest step was inorganic: in June 2025 the Company acquired the structural assets of Telco Enterprises in the United States for about USD 14 million, now operating as Ascent Structural LLC, which extends the American platform from metal building systems into fabricated structural steel and adds capacity in Alabama; Pennar Global Investments Alabama LLC was incorporated in the same month to hold the assets, and the business is already contributing to revenue. Automation was the second thrust: an AGT robotics welding line was commissioned in the United States, automating end plate fitment and stiffener welding - work that previously absorbed twenty to thirty people per product and now requires two, at higher precision and materially lower man hours per tonne - while in India automation was extended across painting, surface treatment and assembly, partly to address labour availability and cost. A dedicated Body in White plant for a marquee automotive customer (Hyundai) reached its final stages of completion during the year, with commissioning expected early in FY 2026-27, after which the vertical will scale as a long cycle OEM programme. At Raebareli, the Company's newest Indian plant, production was streamlined and output taken to the 1,200 MT mark, establishing it as the springboard for northern and eastern India; in PEB India capacity is being added in fabrication and painting lines with utilisation targeted at about 80 per cent against a 70 per cent exit for FY26. In the ZAP91 Solar India joint venture (45 per cent held, with Zetwerk) the Company made a final equity contribution to fund completion and commissioning of the solar module manufacturing plant at Sadashivpet, Telangana, targeted before 30 June 2026, with the module technology upgraded to the G12R format during project execution and no further capital commitment from Pennar envisaged. Two structural moves reshaped the perimeter: the entire 51 per cent holding in Enertech Pennar Defense and Engineering Systems Private Limited was divested in September 2025 as a non-prioritised business, and Pennar FZCO acquired Agile Traders FZCO in December 2025 to build a West Asia trading and distribution platform. Looking forward, planned capex for FY 2026-27 is deliberately light at under Rs 100 crore, principally the completion of the Body in White plant and further automation, to be funded from internal accruals.

risks.risk: Commodity price risk - steel is the dominant input
risks.note: Steel is both the principal input and the substrate of value addition, so the whole cost base moves with it; steel price volatility during FY26 was accentuated by energy price inflation and, per the MD&A threat list, commodity and energy price inflation aggravated by the West Asia conflict continues to pressure input costs and requires continuous pass-through. Mitigation is through price variation clauses in project contracts, pass-through pricing and inventory planning - which are contractual and timing devices, not immunity, and an inventory build ahead of announced price increases was itself a working-capital cost during the year.

risks.risk: Working capital and receivables intensity inherent to project-led businesses
risks.note: Named a Weakness in the SWOT and a Threat in its own right (elevated working capital intensity with attendant borrowing costs). At the year end net working capital stood at 82 days of revenue against the Company's own 75-day target, receivables increased by Rs 151 crore with a portion tied to project sites awaiting handover formalities, and debtor days moved from 65 to 66. Operating cash flow fell year on year specifically because of this working-capital absorption. Mitigation is a defined reduction programme targeting 75 days, site handover completion and collection focus.

risks.risk: Leverage temporarily above the internal comfort level
risks.note: Gross borrowings rose and the gross debt to equity ratio moved to 1.05 from 0.92, driven by about USD 14 million of acquisition funding for Ascent Structural plus working capital borrowing that scaled with revenue and a planned inventory build. Management calls this 'not a number we are comfortable with' and has committed to bringing it to 0.8 or below during FY 2026-27 through internal accruals, the promoter warrant infusion and working capital release. Net of record cash balances gearing was materially lower, but the commitment is unfulfilled and depends on three levers, only one of which is fully within management's control.

risks.risk: Trade policy and tariff risk in export markets
risks.note: Demonstrated rather than hypothetical: United States tariffs disrupted hydraulics export order flows during FY26 - described as the one place in the portfolio where trade policy had a direct effect on the business model - and the backlog fell to Rs 22 crore before recovering to about Rs 34 crore. The structural mitigation is that the largest American revenue stream, metal buildings, is manufactured within the United States and was therefore not exposed; the residual exposure sits in cross-border shipment, which the Company is diversifying towards Europe and West Asia.

risks.risk: Labour availability and rising labour cost in both India and the United States
risks.note: Also demonstrated: labour availability constrained fabrication throughput in Pre Engineered Buildings India in the earlier part of FY26, holding back output and deferring revenue. Resolution required a wider contractor network, wage benchmarking and buffer manning - and management states that securing that manning required paying more, which carries a modest cost to operating margin until automation matures. The Chairman frames the underlying structural issue as the narrowing of the labour cost arbitrage Indian manufacturing has long enjoyed. In the United States, senior management and engineering talent is described as expensive.

risks.risk: Market cyclicality and competitive capacity additions, particularly in PEB
risks.note: The businesses sit on infrastructure, construction and mobility cycles. The MD&A flags intensifying competition in PEB alongside industry capacity additions, which can pressure pricing in the short term. Mitigation is the two-segment, multi-vertical portfolio across geographies and end markets and the rising share of recurring OEM and services revenue - but the SWOT also concedes that scale in individual verticals sits below that of the largest single-vertical competitors.

A growing share of revenue and assets is denominated in US dollars and euros - international markets were 24.1 per cent of FY26 revenue, up from 20 per cent, and the overseas subsidiaries contributed Rs 959.62 crore. Mitigation is forward cover, natural hedges from local manufacture and monitoring of translation effects; FY26 recorded a favourable translation movement in other comprehensive income, which is a reminder that the movement can run the other way. The US buildings platform's growth also depends on a single demand theme - data centre and industrial construction - and is geographically confined to the South and Midwest by plant location.

risks.risk: Regulatory risk - implementation of the Labour Codes
risks.note: The four Labour Codes notified in November 2025 mark a structural reform of the employment law framework. The Company has assessed the indicative financial impact but the effect will only be given as final Central and State rules are notified, so the quantum and timing remain outside its control and the financial impact will be recognised as rules are finalised.

one-line thesis: Pennar delivered record FY26 revenue (INR 3,666 cr) and PAT (INR 139 cr) driven by US data center demand and a strategic mix shift to high-margin businesses, resolving prior labor bottlenecks to target 20% PAT growth in FY27. demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Public capital expenditure in India remains the principal demand engine: the Union Budget for 2026-27 provides a capital outlay of Rs 12.22 lakh crore, up about 11.5 per cent, with Rs 2.81 lakh crore to Railways and Rs 3.10 lakh crore to Road Transport and Highways.
- Manufacturing gross value added grew 10.7 per cent and construction 7.4 per cent in FY26 - the two sectors that most directly drive demand for engineered steel products, pre engineered buildings, tubes and industrial components.
- The Indian pre engineered buildings market is projected by industry studies to grow at roughly 12 per cent a year over the coming decade, with demand broadening beyond warehousing and logistics into data centres, semiconductor and electronics fabrication, solar module plants, food processing and general manufacturing, aided by PLI schemes, PM Gati Shakti and state industrial corridor programmes.
- Speed of construction, cost certainty, superior quality control and sustainability continue to shift share from conventional construction towards factory fabricated steel buildings.
- The sustained United States capital expenditure cycle, led by data centres, manufacturing reshoring and industrial construction, continues to expand the addressable market for the metal buildings businesses; the addressable market exceeds USD 10 billion annually and data centre annualised spending crossed USD 50 billion, overtaking conventional office construction.
- Vehicle lightweighting, electrification and tightening crash and emission regulation are reshaping body structure requirements towards high strength and ultra high strength steels and modular architectures, playing directly to Body in White, hydraulics and precision tubes capabilities; the Indian auto component industry grew 12.7 per cent with OEM supplies up 16.3 per cent.
- Tightening emission norms and rising fuel costs favour energy efficient combustion technologies such as AFBC and waste heat recovery, sustaining replacement demand for boilers, waste heat recovery systems and heat exchangers across food processing, rice milling, chemicals, textiles, distilleries and metals.
- Indian Railways' sustained modernisation and capacity expansion programme, with a record capital outlay and an expanded pipeline of high speed corridors, dedicated freight infrastructure and modern rolling stock.
- AI-assisted design is reshaping engineering services economics by automating lower-end detailing man hours while raising the premium on engineering judgement, project management and statutory certification; because billing is project-outcome based, productivity gains accrue to the service provider - management views this as a structural tailwind rather than a threat.
- Mechanisation across construction, material handling, agriculture, mining and rail, with electro-hydraulic systems, IoT-enabled predictive maintenance and smart sensors, underpins hydraulics demand.
- India's solar build-out - a record 44 GW added in FY26 taking cumulative capacity to about 150 GW - with domestic module manufacturing scaling under the ALMM regime and production linked incentives.
- Margin lever: revenue mix migration towards prioritised, higher-margin businesses, with gross margins in the region of 42 to 43 per cent supported by value added mix despite commodity price inflation in the second half.
- Margin lever: operating leverage on a contained fixed cost base as capacity utilisation rises in PEB India and in the United States.
- Cost headwind flagged: securing PEB manning required paying more, which carries a modest cost to operating margin until automation matures; and the labour cost arbitrage Indian manufacturing has long enjoyed is narrowing.
- Steel price volatility, accentuated by energy price inflation, is managed through price variation clauses in the order book and pass-through pricing.
- Trade policy is a two-sided driver: tariff shifts in the United States affect exports, but manufacturing presence within the United States insulates the bulk of American revenue - the one affected stream, hydraulics, has recovered.
- Return on capital employed moderated as recently deployed capital, including the acquisition and the Body in White facility, is yet to contribute full-year earnings; the medium term objective of raising ROCE remains unchanged.
- Global growth is projected by the IMF to moderate to 3.1 per cent in 2026 before recovering to 3.2 per cent in 2027, with the near term outlook shaped by the conflict in West Asia and the resultant volatility in energy prices.
- Pre Engineered Buildings India closed FY26 with an order backlog of Rs 810 crore, with quote activity healthy and exit capacity utilisation of 70 per cent.
- The combined order backlog of Ascent Buildings and Ascent Structural in the United States stood at about USD 63 million at year end, having grown roughly 20 per cent in the closing three months of the year.
- The boilers and process equipment business entered FY 2026-27 with an order backlog of about Rs 145 crore, its highest ever, with the backlog growing at double digit rates through the closing months.
- The hydraulics order backlog recovered from Rs 22 crore to about Rs 34 crore over the closing months of the year as United States tariff disruption moderated and customers resumed ordering.
- Orders worth Rs 902.26 crore were received across business verticals in the fourth quarter alone.
- An order of approximately Rs 150 crore was declined during the year in PEB India because the product mix did not meet the Company's requirements.
- The boilers business secured its highest capacity orders to date - a 100 tonne per hour AFBC boiler and an 80 tonne per hour waste heat recovery boiler.
- PEB India orders in the closing quarter came from Reliance, JSW Steel, ENES Textiles, Kaizen Industries, Toyo Engineering, MRO Air India, SEMAC Construction, Chalimeda Feeds, Sri Venkateswara Aerospace and Powermech, among others.
- United States buildings customers include KBM Marine, Southeast Construction, Ata Steel and Joist, Ordner Construction, Welbro, JA Street and Associates, Hayden Construction, Joiner Construction, Flintco, M B Kahn Construction, Solomon Associates and LF Jennings.

capital_allocation.body: Disciplined deployment into high-ROCE businesses (PEB US, Boilers). Working capital optimization target: reduce days from 82 to 75. Debt-equity target <0.8x by FY27 end (currently ~0.98x gross, lower net of cash).

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: FY26 was a year of portfolio surgery rather than greenfield capacity building. The largest step was inorganic: in June 2025 the Company acquired the structural assets of Telco Enterprises in the United States for about USD 14 million, now operating as Ascent Structural LLC, which extends the American platform from metal building systems into fabricated structural steel and adds capacity in Alabama; Pennar Global Investments Alabama LLC was incorporated in the same month to hold the assets, and the business is already contributing to revenue. Automation was the second thrust: an AGT robotics welding line was commissioned in the United States, automating end plate fitment and stiffener welding - work that previously absorbed twenty to thirty people per product and now requires two, at higher precision and materially lower man hours per tonne - while in India automation was extended across painting, surface treatment and assembly, partly to address labour availability and cost. A dedicated Body in White plant for a marquee automotive customer (Hyundai) reached its final stages of completion during the year, with commissioning expected early in FY 2026-27, after which the vertical will scale as a long cycle OEM programme. At Raebareli, the Company's newest Indian plant, production was streamlined and output taken to the 1,200 MT mark, establishing it as the springboard for northern and eastern India; in PEB India capacity is being added in fabrication and painting lines with utilisation targeted at about 80 per cent against a 70 per cent exit for FY26. In the ZAP91 Solar India joint venture (45 per cent held, with Zetwerk) the Company made a final equity contribution to fund completion and commissioning of the solar module manufacturing plant at Sadashivpet, Telangana, targeted before 30 June 2026, with the module technology upgraded to the G12R format during project execution and no further capital commitment from Pennar envisaged. Two structural moves reshaped the perimeter: the entire 51 per cent holding in Enertech Pennar Defense and Engineering Systems Private Limited was divested in September 2025 as a non-prioritised business, and Pennar FZCO acquired Agile Traders FZCO in December 2025 to build a West Asia trading and distribution platform. Looking forward, planned capex for FY 2026-27 is deliberately light at under Rs 100 crore, principally the completion of the Body in White plant and further automation, to be funded from internal accruals.

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: Confident and disciplined; Emphasizes 'right to win' in specific segments; Transparent on labor/capex challenges; Committed to 20% PAT growth despite macro noise.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Portfolio diversification across eight divisions and two near-equally sized segments (50.5 per cent and 49.5 per cent of revenue) serving different demand cycles, so a difficult period in one half is ordinarily cushioned by the other - cited as the principal reason the earnings line has risen in each of the last four years.
- Fully integrated engineering capability - design, tooling, manufacturing, project management and erection are held in-house, allowing a customer to present a functional requirement rather than a drawing and receive a commissioned asset.
- Deliberate mix management: roughly 65 to 70 per cent of revenue comes from prioritised businesses growing materially above the Company average, while the remaining 30 to 35 per cent receives no growth capital and is allowed to decline; margin expansion has followed from mix change rather than pricing.
- US manufacturing footprint (Tennessee and Alabama) means the largest American revenue stream, metal buildings, is made within the United States and was not exposed to import tariff action - a different risk profile from cross-border shipment.
- Long growth runway in the United States: the addressable metal buildings and components market exceeds USD 10 billion a year and the Company's share is under 3 per cent, with the binding constraint being plant location rather than customer acceptance.
- Eight management system certifications spanning general quality, environment, occupational health and safety, welding, rail, automotive and aerospace - certification being a condition of entry to several industries served.
- Engineering services bills predominantly on a project outcome basis rather than man hours, so AI-assisted design productivity gains accrue to the Company rather than the customer, while engineering judgement and the statutory professional engineer's certification are not amenable to automation.
- Validation laboratories, material testing protocols and precision-led processes hold output to a common standard across locations, allowing the Company to serve global supply chains from more than one geography.
- Long-standing marquee customer relationships across verticals - Reliance, JSW Steel, Toyo Engineering, MRO Air India and Powermech in PEB; WABCO, Emerson, Endurance, IFB and Xylem in industrial components; Toyota Boshoku, Thermax and ALF Engineering in precision tubes; Saint Gobain, Schaeffler and VECV in steel profiles.
- Industrial harmony and cost visibility: three-year wage agreements signed at the Chennai, Tarapur and Hyderabad plants, and the Best Management Award in the large scale category from the Labour Department, Government of Telangana for 2026.

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body: Working capital bloating (debtor/inventory days up); Labor availability in India requiring costly automation; Raw material price volatility; Execution risk on large boiler orders; US tariff/policy changes.

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body: Management explicitly rejected a INR 150 cr order to protect product mix/margins, signaling a shift from top-line chasing to quality growth. AI is framed as a margin-accretive tool for design detailing rather than a disruption threat.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Run a deliberately balanced two-segment, eight-division portfolio serving independent demand cycles, so that a slowdown in one division is seldom a slowdown across the portfolio - stated to be by design, and cited as a principal reason the earnings line has risen in each of the last four years.
- Concentrate growth capital on 'prioritised' businesses, which are roughly 65 to 70 per cent of revenue and grow materially above the Company average, while giving no growth capital to legacy steel and solar EPC streams and allowing them to decline as a share of revenue; margin expansion is to come from …

other.body:

- [Corporate history] Incorporated 1975 as a private limited company; Pennar Steel Ltd acquired Nagarjuna Steel Ltd and converted into Pennar Industries Ltd (1998); Pennar Engineered Building Systems Ltd incorporated (2008); Pennar Enviro Ltd and PEBS merged into Pennar Industries (2017); US engineering-services presence built via subsidiary Pennar Global Inc (2019); Ascent Buildings LLC (2020).

themes.title: Data-Center & AI electrical/cooling buildout
themes.need: AI/data-center capex pulls transformers, switchgear, gensets, HVAC/cooling, optical and cabling AND a new high-margin cooling supply chain. CUMMINSIND flags DC at ~30-35% of domestic powergen with a demand surge since Oct-2025; VENUSPIPES won a ~INR185cr DC-cooling LOI; AEROFLEX building liquid-cooling skids; BLUESTARCO on DC MEP; STLTECH/NETWEB on optical + HPC/AI servers (STLTECH's DC+Enterprise mix hit 21% of Q1FY27 revenue from 1% in FY26 on record INR13,100cr quarterly order intake anchored by a $1.1bn multi-year hyperscaler deal; FY27 EBITDA-margin guide raised 20%->23% and DC+Enterprise mix guide raised 30%->50% of revenue); REDINGTON/DCI/IVALUE on GPU/AI-infra distribution. Q1FY27 added two balance-sheet-scale entrants: HCLTECH is putting up to INR 3,500cr into its own AI-datacenter business with a 50MW long-term ambition ('megawatt isn't the product, it's the anchor'), and RELIANCE disclosed a 168 MW Meta data centre at Jamnagar built on its own balance sheet.
